title: Why the Son Is Called Word and Flesh
english: John presents him as the maker of all things, and so he gives him the name Word. As a rule, every act of craftsmanship depends on reason, so there was no other way to show that he is the maker of all, for craft is a productive state guided by sound reason. The Son of God is himself none other than a craftsman working with wisdom and skill, and so he is fittingly called Word. He does not make existing things through the Word as though he were a different being from the Word. He himself is the one who makes them, since he is God, the Word.

Since this Word, who is God in being and who is himself the Son of God, became man for the salvation of men, the Word was called "flesh." Some have fallen from true faith, and they think he exists only from the moment when he came forth as man from the Virgin. Against people who think this, John the Evangelist writes most rightly, "In the beginning was the Word" (John 1:1). John uses the verbs with exact fitness, "became" for the flesh and "was" for his divinity.

"Is" would have been the more exact word for the Word of God. But John was declaring the existence of the Word in distinction from the becoming man that happened at a particular time, so the Evangelist used "was" instead of "is." Yet we must not take the ordinary meanings of such verbs when they are used of eternal things. Those meanings apply when what is meant has an existence measured by time: "was" means what no longer exists but once did, "is" likewise means what exists now, and "will be" means what is yet to exist.

title: The Word as Wisdom and Creator
english: But the Word of God is eternal. And he tabernacled among us, and he received this very name, God with us. When he created, because he was not sent by the Father as a man, he brought all things into being. He was with God, and he was God.

The Son of God is also called Wisdom. According to the book of Proverbs, he was created as the beginning of God's ways. Why? Because the Wisdom of God, existing as the wisdom of the one whose wisdom it is, had no relation to anything else. But by God's good pleasure it willed that creatures should come into existence. This Wisdom therefore willed to take up a creative relation toward the things that were to be. This is what is made clear by its having been created as the beginning of God's ways. Along these ways he travels, ordering beings, providing, benefiting, and graciously giving, in this created Wisdom.

They say, then, that the Word is the beginning. He is not other than Wisdom in substance, but only in conception and relation. so that the same existence which the Scriptures now name as to substance is Wisdom insofar as it is at home with God, and the creative Word insofar as it has inclined, so to speak, toward the creatures.

Nor is the Son of God called Word only here. It is possible to cite passages not only from the New Testament but also from the Old: For by the word of the Lord the heavens were made firm, and He sent his word and healed them.
